component: Redundant contextual navigation overlay: floating Back to puzzle button above the phone bottom navigation bar (PuzzleStudyReturnBar.vue)

screenshots.note: Before: floating "Back to puzzle" button above the existing bottom bar, which still shows Notebooks. Two navigation regions, and an element floating over the editor area.
After: the bar has the same width and item count; "Back to puzzle" with a back arrow takes the Notebooks slot. Nothing floats, no placeholder is left.
After, second state of the same screen (see the e2e puzzleStudy.mjs, 185 checks at 360, 390, 414, 430 and 820 wide).

explanation: CaissaTrainer Phase 4 (frontend/src/components/notes/PuzzleStudyReturnBar.vue, route /notes/page/:pageId?study=...; the phone bottom bar is MobileBottomNavComponent). Owner's candidate name: "Redundant contextual navigation overlays". OBSERVED (before, study-return-floating-390.png, 390x844): Puzzle Study Mode (a notebook page opened from an active training puzzle) showed a floating "Back to puzzle" button above the phone's existing bottom navigation bar, which still showed the Notebooks item. The screen therefore had two navigation regions at the bottom edge, one fixed bar and one floating button over the content just above it. PROBLEMS: (1) an extra visual element floating over content; (2) it competes with the navigation hierarchy, since the person sees two places that move them somewhere else and has to decide which is which; (3) it occupies mobile screen space, the least available resource at 390 wide, and the page had to reserve room at its end so the last line could scroll above it; (4) it can overlap content or other controls (it floated over the editor area, and its position had to be tuned by measurement, see FB-0043); (5) two places for related actions: the way back to the puzzle and the way to Notebooks lived in different regions that do the same job (navigate away from this page). CORRECTION (after, study-return-bottom-bar-390.png and study-return-bottom-bar-390-b.png): up to 1024px wide the floating overlay is not rendered. The same action ("Back to puzzle", back arrow icon) takes the slot the Notebooks item has in the existing bottom bar, so the bar gains no item and no placeholder is left, and the action calls the same return logic as before. Outside study mode the bar shows Notebooks again. The explanatory one sentence (shown only when the return reopens the puzzle unscored) appears once at the top of the page, not as an overlay. On wide windows (above 1024px) the floating control stays: no existing navigation region fits it there, and it sits below dialogs and drawers (FB-0043). VERIFIED by frontend/e2e/puzzleStudy.mjs (185 checks, mocked backend) at 360x740, 390x844, 414x896, 430x932 and 820. PREFERRED SOLUTION (general): integrate a contextual navigation action into the existing navigation surface (a bottom bar, a top bar, a sidebar) when that keeps clarity and discoverability: the contextual action takes the slot of the item it temporarily replaces, adds no item and no placeholder, and the surface returns to normal when the context ends. EXCEPTIONS where a floating action is genuinely necessary: (a) there is no existing navigation region at that size (the wide layout here); (b) a primary creation action; (c) an action that must stay reachable while the navigation region is scrolled away or hidden; (d) a safety critical action; (e) a temporary undo or snackbar. TRADEOFF, stated honestly: the replaced item (Notebooks) is not in the bar while study mode lasts. It remains reachable through the application drawer and through ordinary Notes, and study mode is temporary and ends with the return, so the cost is small; but a different product could have a slot nobody can give up, and then a floating control or a different place is the right answer. The owner may decide the slot swap is not appropriate in general. APPROVED GUIDANCE READ (v0.1.0, exact text from guidance/principles.json, PRINCIPLES.md, guidance/antipatterns, guidance/checks/rules.json). P05 Information Must Earn Its Place, summary: "Show the minimum information needed for the current task." Rules: "Do not explain familiar concepts because space is available." and "Prefer familiar patterns, clear naming, predictable position, progressive disclosure and contextual help over permanent explanation." It is about information and copy, not about duplicate navigation; it supports only the small point that the explanatory sentence belongs once on the page and not in an overlay. P10 Minimalism Over Prevalence, summary: "Do not show every possible action at once." Rules: "Prefer contextual and dynamic controls." "Put 'Create' inside the dropdown where it becomes relevant, not beside it." Exception: "Two actions that can genuinely be used at the same moment may both be visible." PRINCIPLES.md: "The objective is fewer visible controls without sacrificing interaction safety." This is the closest approved text on visible controls and it supports the correction in spirit: the bar plus the overlay showed two ways out at once. Its examples (Create inside a dropdown, Send and Stop) are about one control, not about two navigation regions. AP-016 and CHK-016 (toolbar of more than 7 icon only buttons, more than 20 visible controls) did not fire: the bar had 4 or fewer items. P14 No Sidebar Stacking, summary: "Never answer sidebar navigation with another full navigation sidebar beside it." Rules: "Secondary context: replace the sidebar content with a back chevron, or split the sidebar into upper and lower regions, or use the primary content region for details." "The rule targets redundant navigation structures only." This is the closest approved text on the idea, because its remedy for secondary context is to put it into the existing navigation surface rather than add a second one. But it is written for sidebars beside a sidebar; AP-011 and CHK-011 detect two left side by side vertical navigation columns and do not apply to a phone bottom bar and a button. A broad reading of "redundant navigation structures" would cover it; the text does not say so. P18 Mobile Navigation Breathing Room, summary: "Do not compress navigation, headings, filters and actions into dense vertical stacks on mobile." Rules: "Leave clear spacing between navigation and primary content." "Scrolling is preferable to compression." "Move secondary controls into a sheet or menu instead of stacking rows." It is about stacks of rows above content; AP-007 and CHK-007 measure the top area at 390 wide (more than 3 control rows, more than 45 percent of the height, gaps under 8px). A button floating above a bottom bar is outside both. CHK-020 (40px effective hit area at 390, no overlap with neighbouring controls) did apply and passed; it says nothing about whether the control should exist. P21 Remove Before Adding, summary: "Meta-principle: when an interface feels unclear, subtract first." Rule: "Ask whether something can be removed, merged, relocated, hidden contextually, represented through hierarchy or revealed only when needed before adding a component." This is the strongest fit in spirit (merge or relocate into the existing bar before adding a floating one). It is a question to ask, not a testable rule, and no anti-pattern or check states the conclusion. P16 Layout Diversity: "Choose layout from the task, user expectations and information architecture." Not violated; a contextual return is a task need. It also means a rule here must not force one navigation layout. AP-008 and AP-009 (opposing actions, Create beside a dropdown) are the same redundancy idea for single controls and do not extend to navigation. No approved anti-pattern or check addresses a floating or duplicate navigation element, or a contextual action competing with an existing navigation region. HONEST CLASSIFICATION: not clearly an application failure to apply. P21 asks the question and P10 and P14 point the same way, so an application that applied them as strongly as possible would probably have found the swap; but none of them states that a contextual navigation action should live in the existing navigation region, and the original design broke no approved sentence and passed CHK-020. It is also not purely a gap, because P10, P14 and P21 are close. Suggested: guidance-gap, small, with an honest alternative that the owner may prefer: guidance-ambiguity (P14 "redundant navigation structures" and P21 read broadly cover it, narrowly do not), settled by a clarification sentence. Generalizes: any product with a bottom or top navigation surface that adds a contextual return, a "Back to results", a "Continue", a temporary mode exit. Product specific, stays in CaissaTrainer: the labels, the 1024px breakpoint, the study context, which item is swapped. RELATIONSHIP TO FB-0043 (persistent contextual return control and its stacking order): this finding AMENDS FB-0043's position. FB-0043 recorded the floating lower right control as the answer and its stacking order below drawers, scrims, toasts and dialogs; that remains correct for the cases where a floating control is needed. The amendment: the control should live in an existing navigation region when one exists, and a floating control is the fallback for when none does. FB-0043's note that on phones the control sits above the context bar, never over it, is superseded by the swap; its layer order, label honesty and keyboard notes stand for the floating form, and the same label, return logic and honesty sentence apply in the bar form. RELATIONSHIP TO FB-0042: that finding was about controls that belong to a primary region (align with its edges). The return control is page level, as FB-0043 already noted, so FB-0042 does not apply; both share the idea that a control must attach to a defined region rather than float at an arbitrary place. Candidate wording is in feedback/proposals/PR-0002/candidate/amendments.md section K6 and is not policy.

classification.rationale: Small gap, with a real alternative. Not clearly an application failure: the original design broke no approved sentence and passed CHK-020; P21 only asks whether something can be merged or relocated before adding a component, P10 prefers fewer visible controls, P14 targets redundant navigation structures but is written for sidebars (AP-011 and CHK-011 detect left side by side columns), P18 and AP-007 are about rows stacked above content (CHK-007 measures the top area at 390). No approved principle, anti-pattern or check says that a contextual navigation action should live in an existing navigation region, nor lists when a floating action is justified. Honest alternative: a guidance-ambiguity settled by a clarification sentence, if the owner reads P14 redundant navigation structures and P21 broadly. Generalizes to any product with a bottom, top or side navigation surface that adds a contextual return or mode exit. Amends FB-0043: the control belongs in an existing navigation region when one exists, floating is the fallback. Owner confirmation needed.
